children.name: Slavic Language Prerequisite
children.desc: Students must complete First-Level language coursework in a Slavic language (depending on their subplan) or test into the intermediate level courses via the Language Center's placement exam before they can continue to the language and literature requirements.

children.name: Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI)
children.desc: Students must take the Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI) in a Slavic language two quarters prior to degree conferral through the Stanford Language Center.

children.name: GPA of 3.0 in core courses and 2.0 in electives

rules.name: Honors thesis and Honors Colloquium presentation
rules.desc:
Students majoring in any DLCL department (i.e., Comparative Literature, French and Italian, German Studies, Iberian and Latin American Cultures, and Slavic Languages and Literatures) who have an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.3 or above and who maintain a 3.5 (GPA) in their major courses, are eligible to participate in the DLCL’s honors program.
See the Honors webpage for more information.
Program Requirements
To earn honors, students must complete a minimum of 9 units (3 units per quarter), submit a thesis, and present at the Honors Colloquium at the end of their senior year.

rules.name: GPA of 3.3 overall and 3.5 in the major
Overview
rules.desc: The Slavic Studies is designed for those students who wish to gain command of a Slavic language or language of Eastern Europe (Yiddish, Hungarian, Romanian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Estonian, etc.) or the former Soviet Union (Kazakh, Sakha, Georgian, Armenian, etc.), and to study the relevant national literary tradition. Emphasis is placed on the linguistic and philological study of literature, as well as the history of Slavic and East European literature and related media in the broader context of cultural development. This major also welcomes students with an interest in Slavic linguistics.

rules.name: Slavic Language
rules.desc: Complete ONE YEAR (three courses) of SECOND-YEAR language coursework or above, or the equivalent, in any Slavic or East European languages or languages of the former Russian empire and/or Soviet bloc.
rules.notes: First-Year language coursework (RUSSLANG 1, 2, & 3, or 1A & 2A, or equivalent) are prerequisites, and will not count toward the major units requirement.

rules.name: 19th-Century Russian and/or East European Literature and History
rules.desc: Students should choose a course from the provided course list or from courses in history, linguistics, politics, or other relevant fields approved by the DUS.

rules.name: 20th-Century Russian and/or East European Literature and History
rules.desc: Students should choose a course from the provided course list or from courses in history, linguistics, politics, or other relevant fields approved by the DUS.

rules.name: Approved electives: Slavic language, study abroad, SLE (up to 10 units), PWR (up to 5 units) or other fields
rules.desc:
Students should use electives to reach the unit minimum requirement to complete the major.

• Coursework within the department. Additional SLAVIC courses at the 100- or 200- level.

• Language coursework. Approved Slavic language courses from the Language Center.

• Overseas Language Studies. Courses taken in language programs abroad may be allowable with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Structured Liberal Education (SLE) courses may contribute a maximum of ten units.

• PWR courses with at least a ‘B’ may contribute a maximum of five units.

• Subject to approval by the Director of Undergraduate Studies, courses from other fields may count if they contribute to the student’s language skills, the ability to interpret literature and other cultural material, or the capacity to analyze societies.

rules.name: Writing in the Major: SLAVIC 146 (5 units, letter grade)
rules.desc: Majors in the Russian Language and Slavic Studies subplans must take this course for five units and for a letter grade.

children.name: Independent Study
children.desc:
In their senior year, students must enroll in at least 5 units of Independent Study to work on a final project reflecting their major coursework.
With the guidance of the Director of Undergraduate Studies, students choose a project (a substantial piece of independent and original writing) from several options, including but not limited to an analytical research essay or a creative project. Students will present this project to members of the department before graduation.

Russian and Philosophy Subplan Policies
rules.desc:
• The Russian and Philosophy subplan requires 67 units. Students interested in this option should review the Philosophy and Literature website.

• Up to 10 units taken in the Philosophy Department may be taken CR/NC or S/NC; the remainder must be taken for a letter grade.

• Substitutions, including transfer credit, are generally not permitted.

• Units devoted to meeting the department’s language requirement are not counted toward the 65-unit requirement.

rules.name: Russian Language
rules.desc: First-Year Russian (RUSSLANG 1, 2, & 3, or 1A & 2A, or equivalent) are prerequisites, and will not count toward the major units requirement.

rules.name: Russian Literature
rules.desc: A student who has completed the SLE sequence (all three quarters) may count up to ten units toward this major. The SLE units can replace one History of Philosophy course and one upper-division Russian course.

rules.name: Aesthetics, Ethics, and Political Philosophy
rules.notes: Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 170 series class.

rules.name: Language, Mind Metaphysics, and Epistemology
rules.desc: Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 180 series classes.

rules.name: History of Philosophy
rules.desc: Students should enroll in at least ONE course from the PHIL100-139 course set.
rules.notes: A student who has completed the SLE sequence (all three quarters) may count up to ten units toward this major. The SLE units can replace one History of Philosophy course and one upper-division Russian course.

rules.name: Russian and Philosophy Subplan Electives
rules.desc: At least 12 units of electives in Russian language and literature chosen in consultation with the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc: Write a 5,000-word paper on a topic of their choosing, serving as the culmination of their work in the field. To write the paper, students must enroll in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member (or affiliate) in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group. The paper must involve philosophy and literature, and the faculty member must approve the topic by the add/drop deadline.

gpa: Majors must earn a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 (B) in core courses and a 2.0 (C) or better in elective courses to receive credit toward the major.
grading: All courses applied to the major must be taken for a letter grade.
policies: Russian & Philosophy subplan: Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 170 series class or the PHIL 180 series class and are never allowed for PHIL 80, SLAVIC 181.
transferPolicy: External language credit is considered but must be approved by the department.
reviewNotes: You choose Slavic Studies, Russian Language and Literature, or Russian and Philosophy, each with its own language, literature, Writing in the Major and capstone courses, for 60 units (67 for Russian and Philosophy). Every course must be letter graded, except up to 10 Philosophy units in Russian and Philosophy. In the first two subplans, more SLAVIC courses at the 100 or 200 level fill the remaining units; approved language, study abroad, SLE (up to 10 units), PWR (up to 5) and other courses are moved in by hand. The language prerequisite, the OPI, your GPA (3.0 in core, 2.0 in electives) and honors are checked by hand.
